title: Ṣarf and naḥw in the Dars-i Niẓāmī
summary: The Indian madrasas begin with Persian primers of ṣarf and naḥw, then read al-Kāfiya with Jāmī's commentary.

sections.heading: The ṣarf primers
paragraphs: The Dars-i Niẓāmī, the curriculum of Farangī Maḥall that spread to Deoband, Barelī and Khayrābād, opens with short Persian books of ṣarf: Mīzān al-ṣarf, Munshaʿib, Ṣarf-i Mīr and Panj ganj. They were printed together in collections of ṣarf and naḥw in the nineteenth century.
Many madrasas of the Wifāq al-Madāris in Pakistan now read Urdu primers in their place, such as ʿIlm al-ṣarf and Irshād al-ṣarf, and teach the patterns from tables learnt by heart.

sections.heading: The naḥw ladder
paragraphs: Naḥw begins with Naḥw-i Mīr of al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī and al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa of ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī, often printed in one volume. It continues with Hidāyat al-naḥw, then Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Kāfiya and Jāmī's commentary on it, al-Fawāʾid al-ḍiyāʾiyya, known simply as Sharḥ Jāmī.
The Nahwi's Indian path follows this order, with the Persian primers taught in English and the Arabic texts shown where a public-domain print exists.

sources.title: Morphology books of Wifāq al-Madāris al-ʿArabiyya, Hazara Islamicus
